misconception.text: The frequency of an oscillation is the time taken for one complete cycle.

correction.text: That is the period. The frequency is the number of cycles in one second, and the two are reciprocals, so a wave of $50\,\text{Hz}$ has a period of $0.02\,\text{s}$.

signal.text: Our own question offers the period as the frequency.

misconception.text: A wave of frequency $50\,\text{Hz}$ has a period of $2\,\text{s}$.

correction.text: The period is the reciprocal of the frequency, $T = 1/f = 1/50 = 0.02\,\text{s}$. Multiplying the two instead of dividing gives the wrong figure.

signal.text: Our own question offers the multiplied reading as an option.

stem.text: The frequency of an oscillation is

options.text: the time for one complete cycle
the number of cycles in one second
the number of cycles in one minute
the distance covered in one cycle

explanation.text: Frequency is cycles per second, measured in hertz. The time for one cycle is the period, and the two are reciprocals.
